title: Main Line with ...c5
intro: Black attacks the centre with ...c5. Build the c3-d4-e3 pyramid, meet ...Qb6 with Qb3, and drop back to g3 against ...Bd6.
variation: d2d4 d7d5 g1f3 g8f6 c1f4 c7c5, d2d4 g8f6 g1f3 d7d5 c1f4 c7c5

lessons.title: Building the pyramid
lessons.summary: Meet ...c5 with e3, c3 and Nbd2.

steps.text: White opens with 1.d4 to claim the centre and prepare a calm, solid set-up.
Play the first three London moves: d4, Nf3 and Bf4.
steps.hint: Queen's pawn, king's knight, then bring the dark-squared bishop to f4.
steps.ifRight: The London bishop is outside the pawn chain.

steps.text: Black strikes at your centre with 3...c5, the most testing reply.
Support d4 and open the diagonal for your light-squared bishop.
steps.ifRight: Your pawn chain is solid and the f1 bishop is free.

steps.text: Black develops and adds pressure on d4 with 4...Nc6.
Complete the pawn pyramid so d4 cannot be shaken.
steps.ifWrong: Play 5.c3 before bringing out your queen's knight.
steps.ifRight: If Black trades on d4 later, exd4 keeps a strong centre.

feedback.b1d2: 5.Nbd2 is playable too, though 5.c3 keeps d4 guarded and stops ...Qb6 tricks right away.

steps.text: Black plays 5...e6 to free the dark-squared bishop.
Develop the queen's knight to its natural London square.
steps.hint: The knight goes to d2, behind the c3 pawn.
steps.ifWrong: Play 6.Nbd2, keeping the c-pawn supported and eyeing e4.
steps.ifRight: Now White is ready for Bd3, castling and Ne5.

lessons.title: Meeting 5...Qb6
lessons.summary: Answer the early queen attack with Qb3.

steps.text: Instead of 5...e6, Black often targets your undefended b2 pawn with 5...Qb6.
Defend b2 and challenge Black's queen at the same time.
steps.hint: Put your queen opposite Black's queen.
steps.ifRight: If Black trades on b3, axb3 opens the a-file for your rook.

feedback.b2b3: b3 weakens your c3 pawn and dark squares. Answer 5...Qb6 with 6.Qb3.

steps.text: Black pushes past with 6...c4, attacking your queen and trying to shut down the queenside.
Step back with your queen while keeping an eye on the b1-h7 diagonal.
steps.hint: Retreat one square along the diagonal.
steps.ifWrong: Play 7.Qc2: the queen is safe and supports e4 later.
steps.ifRight: White can develop Nbd2, Be2 and strike later with e4 or b3.

feedback.b3b6: Trading on b6 hands Black an open a-file for nothing. Step back to c2.

steps.text: Watch out if Black now attacks your queen with 7...Bf5.
Do not fall for the pawn trap on f5. Move the queen to safety.
steps.hint: Retreat to the back rank, keeping b2 guarded.
steps.ifWrong: Play 8.Qc1: taking on f5 lets Black play ...Qxb2.
steps.ifRight: White stays solid and keeps the extra tempo.

feedback.c2f5: 8.Qxf5 loses after 8...Qxb2, trapping your rook on a1.

steps.text: Here Black traded queens with 6...Qxb3. Recapture to activate your rook.
steps.ifWrong: Play 7.axb3 to open the a-file for your rook.
steps.ifRight: Your a1 rook gets an open file for free.

lessons.title: Meeting ...Bd6 and ...cxd4
lessons.summary: Retreat Bg3 against ...Bd6 and take back with exd4.

steps.text: Black often challenges your strong dark-squared bishop with 6...Bd6.
Keep your bishop on the active diagonal.
steps.ifWrong: Play 7.Bg3: if Black takes, hxg3 opens the h-file.
steps.ifRight: The bishop stays active and White invites ...Bxg3.

feedback.f4d6: Trading on d6 helps Black develop the queen. Step back to g3.

steps.text: Black castles: 7...O-O.
Develop your light-squared bishop to its best attacking square.
steps.ifWrong: Play 8.Bd3, eyeing h7 and preparing castling.
steps.ifRight: White is ready to castle and jump into e5.

steps.text: Sometimes Black takes early with 4...cxd4. Recapture to open your bishop and the e-file.
steps.ifWrong: Play 5.exd4 so your f1 bishop develops freely and your rook eyes the e-file.
steps.ifRight: Next come c3, Bd3, Nbd2 and castling.

feedback.f3d4: Taking with the knight lets Black gain space with ...Nc6 and ...e5 later. Recapture with the pawn.

steps.text: After 4.e3 Nc6 5.c3 cxd4, choose the better recapture to keep your structure healthy.
steps.hint: Keep your centre compact by taking with the e-pawn.
steps.ifWrong: Play 6.exd4: it opens the e-file and leaves no backward pawn on e3.
steps.ifRight: Solid structure, easy development with Bd3 and O-O.

feedback.c3d4: 6.cxd4 leaves the c-file open for Black and keeps your e3 pawn passive. Play 6.exd4.
